hypothesis: If all living things share chemical composition, cellular structure and growth/reproduction machinery, then a substantial set of protein families (e.g. ribosomal proteins, RNA polymerase, aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, DNA replication and cell-division proteins) will be present in nearly every reference proteome across Archaea, Bacteria and Eukaryota.
pass_criterion: Using the reference proteomes grouped by domain (Archaea, Bacteria, Eukaryota) and a fixed family assignment (e.g. Pfam via the proteome annotations), at least 30 protein families are each found in at least 95% of reference proteomes in each of the three domains, and at least 90% of those families are in housekeeping functions (translation, transcription, replication).
fail_criterion: Fewer than 10 protein families are present in at least 95% of reference proteomes in every domain, or the families shared by all three domains do not include components of translation, transcription and replication.
interpretation: Darwin's "chemical composition, germinal vesicles, cellular structure, laws of growth and reproduction" is read as molecular and cellular machinery common to all cellular life. Chemical composition maps to shared biomolecule-producing enzymes and proteins. Cellular structure and growth/reproduction map to ribosome, polymerase and replication/division proteins. Germinal vesicle is the nucleus of the egg, which only eukaryotes have, so it cannot be tested universally and is treated as a nuclear/germ-cell analogue. Viruses are excluded as non-cellular; this is a modern reinterpretation. The test checks only for shared protein families, not for the poison-response example.

dataset.name: Reference Proteomes (UniProt Knowledgebase, current release)
dataset.why_it_fits: The directory is split into Archaea, Bacteria, Eukaryota and Viruses. Per-proteome FASTA and annotation files can be used to count family presence across domains. The README and STATS files give proteome-level metadata. The page title is the FTP directory index, not a named dataset page. It has no DOI.
